commentary_segments.text: The nonlinearity of the expression of V versus OUT V is clearly visible in the IN transfer characteristic. If the Bulk can be connected to the Source (c=0) then the slope of the characteristic is unity: the Source follower has a unity gain. If however, the Bulk is connected to ground (c>0) then clearly the curve is very nonlinear. A lot of distortion is then generated. In addition, it is not clear what the gain is, as the slope depends on the DC biasing voltages. It is preferable that this stage is never used. In a n-well CMOS process, only pMOST source followers can be used, provided their Bulk is connected to the Source.

connection_description_excerpts.text: If the Bulk can be connected to the Source (c=0) then the slope of the characteristic is unity: the Source follower has a unity gain.
If however, the Bulk is connected to ground (c>0) then clearly the curve is very nonlinear.
In a n-well CMOS process, only pMOST source followers can be used, provided their Bulk is connected to the Source.
